legal_activation_condition: covered foreign-provider digital-service supply to Malaysian consumer under SToDS; FSP/platform status and registration threshold apply
operational_control_condition: customer-location evidence and supply/payment relationship are part of administration
what_this_can_explain: why the provider/platform enters the formal SToDS compliance path
what_this_cannot_explain: why Malaysia chose this model over alternative nodes or whether it minimizes compliance cost

legal_activation_condition: DGT designation/appointment is required before the actor carries the PMSE collector duty
operational_control_condition: actor operates within PMSE transaction infrastructure and can issue transaction-linked collection proof
what_this_can_explain: why not every digital actor is automatically a PMSE collector and why appointment status matters
what_this_cannot_explain: the political/administrative reason a particular eligible actor is appointed or the causal effect of appointment

legal_activation_condition: covered household/individual seller activity occurs on an e-commerce/digital platform with online ordering and payment functionality
operational_control_condition: platform directly participates in ordering/payment and can withhold at confirmed successful transaction
designation_or_registration_gate: platform-function gate rather than discretionary designation in the coded path
what_this_can_explain: why transaction-level withholding is assigned to the payment-capable platform in this instrument
what_this_cannot_explain: whether payment control was the legislature's sole motivation or whether the design improves compliance

legal_activation_condition: foreign provider is the baseline liable actor; platform liability applies where the platform performs the statutory continuous process from offering through payment to delivery
operational_control_condition: platform must control the continuous commercial process specified in section 82/13/guidance
what_this_can_explain: when liability shifts from provider to platform and supplies a direct boundary case for the framework
what_this_cannot_explain: whether the shift improves enforcement or why the legislature chose the exact continuous-process test

legal_activation_condition: NRDSP supplies covered digital service to Philippine non-VAT-registered consumer
operational_control_condition: provider controls the supply and must register/remit through the NRDSP rail
what_this_can_explain: why the provider remains the fiscal node for the B2C path even in a digital-market setting
what_this_cannot_explain: whether provider remittance is superior to buyer or marketplace collection

legal_activation_condition: covered purchase is made by a VAT-registered Philippine buyer from an NRDSP
operational_control_condition: buyer/payment relationship and VAT-registered status activate withholding/reverse-charge responsibility
what_this_can_explain: why the buyer rather than the nonresident provider/marketplace carries the B2B remittance path
what_this_cannot_explain: why this node was normatively preferred or its compliance effect

legal_activation_condition: marketplace liability applies only for statutorily specified nonresident-seller transactions where marketplace control conditions are satisfied
operational_control_condition: marketplace must satisfy the legal control/facilitation conditions for the specified supply path
what_this_can_explain: why marketplace liability is conditional rather than universal and how it differs from B2B/B2C paths
what_this_cannot_explain: complete economic control by all marketplaces or performance superiority
